Interestingly, when testing a different 4.7.2 exported Mobile renderer Godot project that is strictly 2D on the same device I get similar startup errors about failing to initialize Vulkan, but the project does not crash. There are some visual glitches, but mostly it appears to run and display as expected. So it might be that some features fail to initialize, but the crash reported above only happens on the first frame if the project utilizes these features rather than during startup as it first appeared.

I've been having the same issue and I found out that the issue stems from a bug in the Vulkan SDK that was fixed in its latest update as seen [here](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/MoltenVK/pull/2758) and [here](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/MoltenVK/releases/tag/v1.4.2). It seems the fix would be updating the Vulkan SDK version used by Godot.

> I've been having the same issue and I found out that the issue stems from a bug in the Vulkan SDK that was fixed in its latest update as seen [here](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/MoltenVK/pull/2758) and [here](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/MoltenVK/releases/tag/v1.4.2). It seems the fix would be updating the Vulkan SDK version used by Godot.

Great find! Have you tested locally that custom builds with MoltenVK 1.4.1 have the build and MoltenVK 1.4.2 fix it?

It would also be helpful to check whether older Godot versions like 4.6.x and 4.5.x have the bug or not. 4.7.x/4.8 use MoltenVK 1.4.1 but earlier releases had a different MoltenVK version. It's not clear to me yet when the MoltenVK regressions were introduced and so which Godot releases are affected.

@Repiteo I opened https://github.com/godotengine/godot-build-scripts/pull/173 to update MoltenVK for official builds, which could be tested on the next 4.8 dev snapshot or 4.7.3 rc.

I've never built Godot before so I may have done something wrong, or my hypothesis was entirely incorrect. I installed the newest version of the Vulkan SDK (1.4.357.1), git cloned the 4.7-stable branch and tried compiling Godot. I got many "___ has no symbols" errors while compiling, and I also got a "ld: warning: object file (/Users/[][][][][][]/VulkanSDK/1.4.357.1/macOS/lib/MoltenVK.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libMoltenVK.a[x86_64][2](libMoltenVK.a-x86_64-prelink.o)) was built for newer 'macOS' version (12.0) than being linked (10.13)" error at the very end of compiling which might have something to do with it. For context, I'm on macOS Sequoia (15). In the end tho, it didn't work and I'm still receiving errors. I also did some backtracking and I know for sure that the bug was introduced somewhere between 4.6.3 and 4.7, but I don't know where. I haven't tested what Vulkan SDK version introduced the bug.

> I've been having the same issue and I found out that the issue stems from a bug in the Vulkan SDK that was fixed in its latest update as seen [here](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/MoltenVK/pull/2758) and [here](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/MoltenVK/releases/tag/v1.4.2). It seems the fix would be updating the Vulkan SDK version used by Godot.

This certainly sounds like it could be the cause for the issues with starting up the vulkan renderer and something that would fix this (if we just then update to the new MoltenVK version?).

However, the second part of the issue still stands. Regardless of why the vulkan renderer failed, shouldn't it then fallback to the OpenGL compatibility renderer instead of just crashing? Isn't that the point of the new automatic fallback system to handle cases like this?

I'm running into this issue as well. Used 4.8dev7 and I'm still crashing with the new version of MoltenVK. Before this I was using 4.5 and it worked, 4.7 is also broken for me.
